subjects.name: Leonardo DiCaprio
clues: Born in Los Angeles in 1974, he started out in TV commercials and a family sitcom.
He earned an early Oscar nomination for playing Johnny Depp's younger brother in a 1993 drama.
A long-time environmental campaigner, he set up his own foundation in 1998.
He played a dream thief in Inception and a teenage con man in Catch Me If You Can.
He played Jack Dawson, the young artist who wins a ticket aboard the doomed liner in Titanic.
subjects.fact: He won his first Oscar in 2016 for The Revenant, on his fifth acting nomination.

subjects.name: Tom Hanks
clues: Born in California in 1956, he first found fame in light comedies of the 1980s.
He played a boy magically turned into a grown-up in the 1988 comedy Big.
He won back-to-back Best Actor Oscars, in 1994 and 1995.
He voiced the cowboy Woody and was stranded with a volleyball in Cast Away.
He played a kind-hearted Alabama man who compares life to a box of chocolates.
subjects.fact: Only he and Spencer Tracy have won the Best Actor Oscar in two consecutive years.

subjects.name: Marlon Brando
clues: Born in Nebraska in 1924, he trained in New York and helped popularise 'method' acting.
He played Stanley Kowalski in A Streetcar Named Desire, both on stage and on film.
He won Best Actor for On the Waterfront, with its famous line about being a contender.
He played Superman's father, Jor-El, in the 1978 film.
He played the mob boss Vito Corleone in The Godfather, winning an Oscar he turned down.
subjects.fact: He sent actress Sacheen Littlefeather to the 1973 Oscars to decline his award in protest.

subjects.name: Tom Cruise
clues: Born in New York State in 1962, he became a star in the 1983 comedy Risky Business.
He played a racing driver in Days of Thunder and a sports agent in Jerry Maguire.
He is famous for doing his own stunts, including climbing the Burj Khalifa in Dubai.
He has played the secret agent Ethan Hunt in a spy series since 1996.
He played the hotshot navy pilot Maverick in Top Gun and its 2022 sequel.
subjects.fact: For Mission: Impossible - Fallout he learned to fly a helicopter for its chase scenes.

subjects.name: Shah Rukh Khan
clues: Born in New Delhi in 1965, he started out in television serials in the late 1980s.
He is famous for an open-armed pose in countless romantic film songs.
In 2023 he led two huge action hits, Pathaan and Jawan.
He played the lovestruck Raj in Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge, a record-breaking romance.
Nicknamed the 'King of Bollywood', he lives in a Mumbai seafront home called Mannat.
subjects.fact: He studied economics at Hansraj College in Delhi before moving to Mumbai.

subjects.name: Amitabh Bachchan
clues: Born in Allahabad in 1942, he is the son of a celebrated Hindi poet.
His tall frame and deep baritone voice became his trademarks.
He became known as the 'angry young man' of 1970s Hindi cinema.
He first hosted Kaun Banega Crorepati, India's Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, in 2000.
He played Jai alongside Dharmendra's Veeru in the 1975 classic Sholay.
subjects.fact: A 1999 BBC online poll named him the greatest star of stage or screen of the millennium.

subjects.name: Jackie Chan
clues: Born in Hong Kong in 1954, he trained for years at a Peking Opera school as a child.
He worked as a stunt extra in Bruce Lee films early in his career.
His action comedies mix kung fu with slapstick, and he performs his own dangerous stunts.
His films often end with blooper reels showing stunts that went wrong.
He teamed up with Chris Tucker in Rush Hour and voiced Monkey in Kung Fu Panda.
subjects.fact: He received an honorary Oscar in 2016 for his lifetime of work.

subjects.name: Bruce Lee
clues: Born in San Francisco in 1940, he grew up in Hong Kong as a child actor.
He played Kato, a masked chauffeur, in the 1960s TV series The Green Hornet.
He created his own martial art, called Jeet Kune Do.
His one-inch punch and lightning-fast nunchucks became legendary.
He starred in Enter the Dragon, released in 1973 just after his sudden death at 32.
subjects.fact: He gave martial arts lessons to Hollywood stars such as Steve McQueen.

subjects.name: Arnold Schwarzenegger
clues: Born in a small Austrian village in 1947, he moved to the United States aged 21.
He won the Mr. Olympia bodybuilding title seven times.
He played a barbarian warrior in Conan and a cop working undercover in Kindergarten Cop.
He served as Governor of California from 2003 to 2011.
He played a robot assassin from the future in The Terminator, promising 'I'll be back'.
subjects.fact: He became a US citizen in 1983, fifteen years after arriving in America.

subjects.name: Morgan Freeman
clues: Born in Memphis, Tennessee, in 1937, he served in the US Air Force before acting.
He was a familiar face on the 1970s children's TV show The Electric Company.
He won an Oscar for Million Dollar Baby and played Nelson Mandela in Invictus.
He played God in Bruce Almighty and is famed for his calm narrating voice.
He played Red, the prisoner who narrates The Shawshank Redemption.
subjects.fact: He narrated the 2005 Oscar-winning documentary March of the Penguins in English.

subjects.name: Robert De Niro
clues: Born in New York City in 1943, he grew up around Greenwich Village and Little Italy.
He played a scary father-in-law opposite Ben Stiller in Meet the Parents.
He gained about 60 pounds to play boxer Jake LaMotta in Raging Bull, winning Best Actor.
He played the young Vito Corleone in The Godfather Part II, winning an Oscar.
He asked 'You talkin' to me?' into a mirror as a New York cab driver in Taxi Driver.
subjects.fact: He co-founded the Tribeca Film Festival in New York in 2002.

subjects.name: Keanu Reeves
clues: Born in Beirut in 1964, he grew up mostly in Toronto, Canada.
He played a time-travelling slacker in Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure.
He played a police officer trapped on a bus that must not slow down in Speed.
He voiced the stuntman toy Duke Caboom in a 2019 Pixar sequel.
He played Neo, the hacker who takes the red pill, in The Matrix.

links.name: Toy Story
links.rel: voiced a role in a sequel to

subjects.fact: His first name is Hawaiian and is often said to mean 'cool breeze over the mountains'.

subjects.name: Toshiro Mifune
clues: Born in 1920 in Qingdao, China, to Japanese parents, he served in the military in the war.
He got into films almost by accident after a friend sent his photo to a studio talent search.
He starred in 16 films for the same great Japanese director.
He played the bandit in Rashomon and a wandering swordsman for hire in Yojimbo.
He played the wild, would-be warrior Kikuchiyo in Seven Samurai.
subjects.fact: He won the Best Actor prize at the Venice Film Festival twice.

subjects.name: Harrison Ford
clues: Born in Chicago in 1942, he worked as a carpenter while struggling as an actor.
He played the US president fighting hijackers aboard his plane in Air Force One.
He played the replicant hunter Rick Deckard in Blade Runner.
He played the smuggler Han Solo, pilot of the Millennium Falcon.
He played the whip-cracking archaeologist Indiana Jones in Raiders of the Lost Ark.
subjects.fact: He returned as Han Solo in The Force Awakens in 2015, 38 years after the first Star Wars film.

subjects.name: Daniel Day-Lewis
clues: Born in London in 1957, he is the son of a British Poet Laureate.
He is famous for staying in character for months while making a film.
He played the painter and writer Christy Brown in My Left Foot.
He played a ruthless oil man in There Will Be Blood and the 16th US president in Lincoln.
He was the first man to win three Best Actor Oscars.
subjects.fact: During a break from acting in the late 1990s, he learned shoemaking in Italy.

subjects.name: Rajinikanth
clues: Born in Bangalore in 1950, he worked as a bus conductor before acting.
He made his film debut in 1975 in a Tamil drama by K. Balachander.
His trademark style tricks, like flipping sunglasses onto his face, delight fans.
He played a scientist and the robot he builds in the 2010 sci-fi hit Enthiran.
Called 'Superstar' and 'Thalaivar' by fans, he is a giant of Tamil cinema.

links.name: Chennai
links.rel: is a star of the film industry of

subjects.fact: His real name is Shivaji Rao Gaikwad.

subjects.name: Marilyn Monroe
clues: Born in Los Angeles in 1926, she spent much of her childhood in foster homes.
She was born Norma Jeane Mortenson and worked in an aircraft factory during World War II.
She won a Golden Globe for the 1959 comedy Some Like It Hot.
She sang 'Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend' in Gentlemen Prefer Blondes.
Her white dress billowing over a subway grate in The Seven Year Itch is iconic.
subjects.fact: She sang a famous breathy 'Happy Birthday' to President John F. Kennedy in 1962.

subjects.name: Audrey Hepburn
clues: Born in Brussels in 1929, she lived through the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands as a girl.
She trained as a ballet dancer before turning to acting.
She won Best Actress for her first starring role, a runaway princess in Roman Holiday.
Later in life she travelled the world as a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador.
She wore a little black dress and pearls as Holly Golightly in Breakfast at Tiffany's.

links.name: Rome
links.rel: starred in a film set in

subjects.fact: She is one of the few people to have won an Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar and a Tony.

subjects.name: Meryl Streep
clues: Born in New Jersey in 1949, she studied acting at the Yale School of Drama.
She won her first Oscar for the 1979 divorce drama Kramer vs. Kramer.
She won Best Actress playing British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher in The Iron Lady.
She played a fearsome fashion magazine editor in The Devil Wears Prada.
By 2024 she had 21 Oscar nominations, more than any other actor.
subjects.fact: She is famous for mastering accents, from Polish to Danish to Australian.

subjects.name: Julia Roberts
clues: Born in Georgia, USA, in 1967, her older brother Eric was also an actor.
She broke through in the 1988 film Mystic Pizza and then in Steel Magnolias.
She won Best Actress playing a legal clerk who took on a power company in Erin Brockovich.
Her wide smile and laugh became trademarks in Notting Hill and Runaway Bride.
She played Vivian opposite Richard Gere in the 1990 hit Pretty Woman.
subjects.fact: Her niece Emma Roberts is also an actress.

subjects.name: Aishwarya Rai
clues: Born in Mangalore in 1973, she briefly studied architecture before modelling.
She made her film debut in Mani Ratnam's Tamil film Iruvar in 1997.
She played Paro in the lavish Devdas, shown at the Cannes Film Festival in 2002.
In 2007 she married actor Abhishek, son of the legendary star of Sholay.
She was crowned Miss World in 1994, launching her film career.
subjects.fact: In 2003 she became the first Indian actress to serve on the jury of the Cannes Film Festival.

subjects.name: Priyanka Chopra
clues: Born in Jamshedpur in 1982, she spent part of her teens at school in the United States.
She won the Miss World title in 2000.
She played the boxer Mary Kom in a 2014 biopic.
She became the first South Asian actor to lead an American network drama, Quantico.
A Miss World turned Bollywood star, she married an American pop singer in 2018.
subjects.fact: She is also a singer and released her first English-language single in 2012.

subjects.name: Nicole Kidman
clues: Born in Hawaii in 1967 to Australian parents, she grew up in Sydney.
She became known as a teenager in the Australian film BMX Bandits.
She played a nightclub star in the musical Moulin Rouge!
She won Best Actress wearing a false nose to play Virginia Woolf in The Hours.
She was married to Tom Cruise, her co-star in Days of Thunder.
subjects.fact: She was the first Australian to win the Best Actress Oscar.

subjects.name: Sophia Loren
clues: Born in Rome in 1934, she grew up in poverty near Naples during the war.
She entered beauty contests as a teenager, which led to her first film roles.
She married the film producer Carlo Ponti.
She won Best Actress for Two Women, the first acting Oscar for a foreign-language role.
This Italian screen icon starred with Marcello Mastroianni in Marriage Italian Style.
subjects.fact: She received an honorary Oscar in 1991 for her career.

subjects.name: Angelina Jolie
clues: Born in Los Angeles in 1975, she is the daughter of actor Jon Voight.
She won a supporting actress Oscar for Girl, Interrupted in 2000.
She played the tomb-raiding adventurer Lara Croft in two films.
She served as a Special Envoy for the UN refugee agency from 2012 to 2022.
She played the horned fairy Maleficent in the 2014 Disney film.
subjects.fact: She has also directed films, including Unbroken in 2014.

subjects.name: Emma Watson
clues: Born in Paris in 1990, she moved to England as a young child.
She was cast in her first film role at the age of nine.
She played Belle in the 2017 live-action Beauty and the Beast.
She became a UN Women Goodwill Ambassador in 2014, launching the HeForShe campaign.
She played the clever young witch Hermione Granger in the Harry Potter films.
subjects.fact: She studied English literature at Brown University in the United States.

subjects.name: Michelle Yeoh
clues: Born in Ipoh, Malaysia, in 1962, she trained in ballet in London.
She was crowned Miss Malaysia in 1983.
She did her own stunts in Hong Kong action films, including one with Jackie Chan.
She played a spy in Tomorrow Never Dies and a warrior in Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon.
She became the first Asian woman to win Best Actress, for Everything Everywhere All at Once.
subjects.fact: She won her Oscar in 2023, aged 60.

subjects.name: Judi Dench
clues: Born in York in 1934, she made her name on stage at the Old Vic and with the RSC.
She starred in the long-running British sitcom As Time Goes By.
She was made a Dame in 1988.
She won an Oscar for about eight minutes on screen as Elizabeth I in Shakespeare in Love.
She played M, head of British intelligence, in the James Bond films from GoldenEye on.

links.name: United Kingdom
links.rel: is a stage and screen star of

subjects.fact: She was the first woman to play M in the James Bond film series.

subjects.name: Elizabeth Taylor
clues: Born in London in 1932 to American parents, she moved to Los Angeles as a child.
She became a child star in National Velvet, riding a horse in a big race.
She was married eight times, twice to the actor Richard Burton.
She won Best Actress for BUtterfield 8 and Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?
She played the Egyptian queen in the lavish 1963 epic Cleopatra.
subjects.fact: She was famous for her striking eyes, often described as violet.

subjects.name: Gong Li
clues: Born in Shenyang, China, in 1965, she trained at Beijing's Central Academy of Drama.
She made her debut in Red Sorghum, which won the Golden Bear in Berlin in 1988.
She worked closely with director Zhang Yimou on films like Raise the Red Lantern.
She starred in Farewell My Concubine, which shared the Palme d'Or in 1993.
She played the rival geisha Hatsumomo in the Hollywood film Memoirs of a Geisha.
subjects.fact: She won the Best Actress prize at the Venice Film Festival in 1992 for The Story of Qiu Ju.

subjects.name: Alfred Hitchcock
clues: Born in London in 1899, he began in silent films designing title cards.
He moved to Hollywood in 1939, and his first film there, Rebecca, won Best Picture.
He made brief cameo appearances in most of his own films.
He hosted a TV mystery series, opening each episode with a dry 'Good evening'.
Called the 'Master of Suspense', he made Psycho, Vertigo and The Birds.
subjects.fact: Despite five Best Director nominations, he never won that Oscar.

subjects.name: Steven Spielberg
clues: Born in Cincinnati, Ohio, in 1946, he made home movies as a boy.
He co-founded the film studio DreamWorks in 1994.
He won Best Director for Schindler's List and Saving Private Ryan.
His 1975 shark thriller is often called the first summer blockbuster.
He directed E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial and Jurassic Park.
subjects.fact: He shot Jaws with a mechanical shark that broke down so often it is rarely seen.

subjects.name: Stanley Kubrick
clues: Born in New York City in 1928, he started out as a photographer for Look magazine.
He moved to England in the 1960s and made his later films there.
He was famous for demanding dozens of takes of a single shot.
His Cold War comedy Dr. Strangelove ends with a man riding a falling bomb.
He directed 2001: A Space Odyssey, with its calm but deadly computer HAL 9000.
subjects.fact: His only Oscar win came for the special effects of 2001: A Space Odyssey.

subjects.name: Akira Kurosawa
clues: Born in Tokyo in 1910, he first trained as a painter.
His film Rashomon won the Golden Lion in Venice in 1951.
He received an honorary Oscar in 1990 for his lifetime of work.
His films inspired the westerns The Magnificent Seven and A Fistful of Dollars.
He directed Seven Samurai, starring his favourite actor Toshiro Mifune.
subjects.fact: George Lucas has said his film The Hidden Fortress helped inspire Star Wars.

subjects.name: Hayao Miyazaki
clues: Born in Tokyo in 1941, his family's company made aircraft parts during the war.
He co-founded an animation studio in 1985 named after a hot desert wind.
His hand-drawn films often feature flying machines, brave young heroines and nature.
His films won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature in 2003 and again in 2024.
He directed My Neighbor Totoro and Spirited Away at Studio Ghibli.
subjects.fact: His second Oscar came for The Boy and the Heron, released in 2023.

subjects.name: James Cameron
clues: Born in Ontario, Canada, in 1954, he drove a truck before making films.
In 2012 he dived alone to the Challenger Deep, the deepest known point of the ocean.
He directed The Terminator and its sequel, Judgment Day.
He made many deep-sea dives to the real wreck of a famous ocean liner.
He directed both Titanic and Avatar, each the highest-grossing film of its time.
subjects.fact: Titanic won him three Oscars in one night: Best Picture, Best Director and Best Editing.

subjects.name: Christopher Nolan
clues: Born in London in 1970, he made short films with his father's Super 8 camera as a boy.
His breakthrough film Memento tells its story backwards.
He prefers real effects, once crashing a real jumbo jet into a building for Tenet.
He directed The Dark Knight trilogy about Batman.
He directed Inception and won Best Director for Oppenheimer.
subjects.fact: He often shoots on IMAX film cameras for huge, sharp images.

subjects.name: Satyajit Ray
clues: Born in Calcutta in 1921, he worked as a graphic designer at an advertising agency.
He also wrote popular children's books, including the Feluda detective stories.
He made his first film on a tiny budget, inspired by the Italian film Bicycle Thieves.
He received an honorary Oscar in 1992, shortly before his death.
He directed the Bengali Apu Trilogy, starting with Pather Panchali in 1955.
subjects.fact: He often wrote the music and designed the posters for his own films.

subjects.name: Martin Scorsese
clues: Born in New York in 1942, he grew up in Little Italy and once planned to be a priest.
Childhood asthma kept him indoors, where he watched films constantly.
He has made many films with Robert De Niro and later with Leonardo DiCaprio.
He finally won Best Director for The Departed in 2007.
He directed Taxi Driver, Raging Bull and Goodfellas.
subjects.fact: He founded The Film Foundation in 1990 to help restore old films.

subjects.name: George Lucas
clues: Born in Modesto, California, in 1944, he dreamed of racing cars until a bad crash.
His 1973 film American Graffiti looked back at teenage life in the early 1960s.
He founded the visual effects company Industrial Light & Magic.
He created the adventurer Indiana Jones with his friend Steven Spielberg.
He created Star Wars and its villain Darth Vader.
subjects.fact: He sold his company Lucasfilm to Disney in 2012.

subjects.name: Peter Jackson
clues: Born in New Zealand in 1961, he made films as a boy with a Super 8 camera.
His first feature was a low-budget comedy shot with friends on weekends.
He remade the giant ape adventure King Kong in 2005.
He brought old First World War footage to life in colour in They Shall Not Grow Old.
He directed The Lord of the Rings trilogy, filmed in his home country.
subjects.fact: The Return of the King won all 11 Oscars it was nominated for.

subjects.name: Bong Joon-ho
clues: Born in Daegu, South Korea, in 1969, he studied sociology at university.
His monster film The Host features a creature from the Han River in Seoul.
He made Snowpiercer, set on a train circling a frozen world.
His film Okja is about a girl and her giant pet pig.
His Parasite was the first non-English language film to win Best Picture.
subjects.fact: Parasite won four Oscars in 2020, including Best Director and Best Picture.

subjects.name: Charlie Chaplin
clues: Born in London in 1889, he spent part of his poor childhood in a workhouse.
He toured America with Fred Karno's comedy troupe before joining films.
He co-founded the United Artists film studio in 1919.
He wrote the music for his own films, including the tune of the song 'Smile'.
His Little Tramp wore a bowler hat, baggy trousers and a small moustache.
subjects.fact: He received an honorary Oscar in 1972 and a 12-minute standing ovation.

subjects.name: Rowan Atkinson
clues: Born in northern England in 1955, he studied electrical engineering at Oxford.
He played the scheming Edmund in the historical comedy Blackadder.
He played a fussy jewellery salesman in Love Actually.
He played a bumbling spy in the Johnny English films.
He created and played the clumsy, almost silent man with a teddy bear and a green Mini.
subjects.fact: He performed as his silent clown character at the London 2012 Olympics opening ceremony.

subjects.name: Robin Williams
clues: Born in Chicago in 1951, he trained at the Juilliard School in New York.
He became famous as an alien from the planet Ork in Mork & Mindy.
He won an Oscar for playing a therapist in Good Will Hunting.
He dressed as an elderly Scottish nanny in Mrs. Doubtfire.
He voiced the wisecracking Genie in Disney's 1992 film Aladdin.
subjects.fact: He improvised so much as the Genie that hours of extra recordings were made.

subjects.name: Jim Carrey
clues: Born in Ontario, Canada, in 1962, he did stand-up comedy as a teenager in Toronto.
He became known on the sketch comedy show In Living Color.
He played a man whose whole life is secretly a TV show in The Truman Show.
He played the green Christmas-hating Grinch in a 2000 film.
His rubbery face made Ace Ventura: Pet Detective and The Mask big hits.
subjects.fact: He won Golden Globes for The Truman Show and Man on the Moon.

subjects.name: Buster Keaton
clues: Born in Kansas in 1895, he performed in his parents' vaudeville act as a toddler.
He was called 'The Great Stone Face' because he almost never smiled on screen.
He did his own stunts, once letting the front of a house fall around him.
His 1926 Civil War comedy The General is about a stolen train.
With Charlie Chaplin, he was a great silent comedy star, known for his flat pork-pie hat.
subjects.fact: He received an honorary Oscar in 1960.

subjects.name: Eddie Murphy
clues: Born in Brooklyn in 1961, he joined Saturday Night Live at just 19.
He played a fast-talking Detroit police officer in Beverly Hills Cop.
He played nearly a whole family under heavy makeup in The Nutty Professor.
He played an African prince looking for a bride in New York in Coming to America.
He voiced the chatty talking Donkey in Shrek.
subjects.fact: He voiced the little dragon Mushu in Disney's 1998 film Mulan.

subjects.name: Oprah Winfrey
clues: Born in rural Mississippi in 1954, she became a TV news anchor in Nashville at 19.
She was nominated for an Oscar for her role in The Color Purple.
She named her production company Harpo, her first name spelled backwards.
Her book club turned many novels into instant bestsellers.
Her daytime talk show ran nationally from 1986 to 2011, making her the 'Queen of Talk'.
subjects.fact: She opened a leadership academy for girls in South Africa in 2007.

subjects.name: David Attenborough
clues: Born in 1926, he joined the BBC in 1952 and later ran its second channel.
His brother Richard was an Oscar-winning film director.
He wrote and presented the landmark series Life on Earth in 1979.
A British polar research ship was named after him.
This much-loved naturalist narrated Planet Earth and Blue Planet.
subjects.fact: He has made programmes for the BBC in every decade since the 1950s.

subjects.name: Ellen DeGeneres
clues: Born in Louisiana in 1958, she began as a stand-up comedian in New Orleans clubs.
She starred in her own self-titled sitcom in the 1990s.
She hosted the Oscars in 2007 and 2014, taking a famous group selfie.
She voiced the forgetful blue fish Dory in Finding Nemo.
Her daytime talk show, famous for dancing and giveaways, ran from 2003 to 2022.
subjects.fact: She received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016.

subjects.name: Johnny Carson
clues: Born in Iowa in 1925, he performed as a teenage magician before serving in the US Navy.
He began his famous late-night hosting run in October 1962.
His comic characters included the turbaned mind reader Carnac the Magnificent.
His farewell in May 1992 ended thirty years at the same desk.
Known as the 'King of Late Night', he hosted The Tonight Show for three decades.
subjects.fact: His opening golf-swing gesture became one of television's most famous habits.
